title: (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Consecutive interpretation in Interpreter agent will be generally available
summary: Consecutive interpretation in Microsoft Teams Interpreter, currently in public preview, will roll out to general availability by late 2026. It offers turn-by-turn AI-generated spoken translation using usage-based billing with Copilot Credits. Organizations must set spending policies and have eligible meeting organizers with Copilot licenses.
body:
Updated November 16, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

Consecutive interpretation in Interpreter for Teams meetings, currently in public preview, is planned to begin rolling out to general availability. This is a new mode in Interpreter that helps meeting participants collaborate more naturally in bilingual conversations. After an eligible meeting organizer turns it on, this turn-by-turn experience interprets each statement after a speaker finishes and then plays the interpreted audio for all meeting participants to hear. 

Similar to other new advanced Microsoft AI experiences, consecutive interpretation will be delivered through usage-based billing (UBB) with Copilot Credits. Usage charges can begin after an administrator configures a spending policy and an eligible meeting organizer turns on the experience for their meeting. A Copilot license is also required as a pre-requisite for the organizer of the meeting. 

The existing simultaneous interpretation mode in Interpreter for Teams meetings and Rooms, which is generally available, hasn't changed. It's still a personal listening experience that includes 20 hours of interpreted audio per month through a Copilot license or a Teams Rooms Pro license. Access beyond the hours included is subject to available capacity, limitations, and additional terms.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557180.

[When this will happen]

- Targeted Release: Rollout begins in early May 2026 (previously early April) and is expected to complete by late May 2026 (previously mid-April).- General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.[How this will affect your organization]

Who is affected: 

Organizations that use Interpreter in Teams meetings, including public preview users of consecutive interpretation. 

- In a meeting, an eligible organizer can select More > Interpreter > Consecutive interpretation (uses credits), then choose the two spoken languages. - Consecutive interpretation waits for each speaker to finish, then provides AI-generated spoken interpretation so that all participants hear the same interpreted speech. Interpretation quality may vary depending on audio quality, participant speech patterns, network conditions, and language pair. - Available in Teams meetings on Windows, Mac and web; not currently supported in Teams Events, calls or Teams Rooms.[What you need to do to prepare]

- You will need to set up spending policies to enable consecutive interpretation for eligible meeting organizers. Learn more: Managing AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing | Microsoft Learn - When the experience is generally available, updates will be published to the Copilot Credits Guide so you can review pricing rates and estimate costs for your organization.- Learn more

  • Available in Teams meetings on Windows, Mac and web; not currently supported in Teams Events, calls or Teams Rooms.
